paper.title: Bayesian Collaborative Bandits with Thompson Sampling for Improved Outreach in Maternal Health Program

settings.name_in_paper: Cluster Model with infinite arms (clustered low rank bandits, Bayesian setup)
unmapped: Multi-user setting: N users arrive uniformly at random; each user belongs to one of C clusters via unknown assignment c:[N]->[C]; reward is R(c(u),:)^T a with unknown cluster-reward matrix R in R^{C x D}
settings.definition_quote: Y(u,a) \sim R(u,:)^T a + N where N is i.i.d 1-sub-Gaussian random variable. ... We further consider \Omega_C with a clustering assumption that is there are only C distinct rows in R and every user u is mapped to a cluster using a cluster assignment function c:[N] \rightarrow [C].

conditions: ||R(u,:)||_2 < S for all R in support of prior
users arrive uniformly at random from [N]
tuning: exact posterior (perfect Gibbs) sampling at every step

source.quote: For the cluster model in the infinite arm case, we have: a) the log-covering number $\log N(\Omega_C, \epsilon, ||.||_\infty) = O(CD \log(1/\epsilon)+ N \log C)$ and, b) $\mathrm{dim}_E(\Omega_C, \epsilon) = \mathcal{O}(2CD \log (1+2S/\epsilon^2) + CN)$ ... Thus propositions 4 and 5 from \cite{russo2013eluder} with $\epsilon = T^{-2}$ yields a Bayesian regret bound of: \tilde{O}(CD\sqrt{T(1+N/D)(1+\log(C)N/(CD))}\log(T))

results.notes: Paper's D is the action dimension (mapped to d). Obtained by plugging the paper's Eluder dimension and covering-number bounds into Russo & Van Roy (2013). Theorems 2, 3, 5, 6 bound the Eluder dimension ((2D+N)C finite arms; O(2CD log(1+2S/eps^2)+CN) infinite arms); they are complexity characterizations, not regret bounds, so not recorded separately. Applies to idealised TS, not TS-SGLD.

cited_results.cited_title: Eluder dimension and the sample complexity of optimistic exploration
cited_results.setting_description: Bayesian regret of Thompson sampling for a general model class, in terms of eluder dimension dim_E and covering number of the class
